hints.title: Check the algebraic identities first
hints.body: Expand <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> independently and then subtract <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math>. Keep the condition that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> is a positive integer when interpreting the resulting expression.
hints.recap: Consecutive positive cube numbers can be represented using consecutive positive integers.
hints.pitfall: A correct final assertion would not by itself validate every line of a proof.

hints.title: Be precise about what a discriminant says
hints.body: Calculate the discriminant of the displayed quadratic. State exactly what this tells you about factoring the polynomial into linear factors.
hints.recap: A quadratic with a negative discriminant has no real linear factors.
hints.pitfall: A polynomial is an expression in a variable; substituting a particular integer produces a number. Keep these two kinds of object distinct.
hints.pause: Compare the precise statements made in successive lines.

recall.reminder: Use a quadratic discriminant only for the conclusion it supports.

hints.title: Test the numerical claim
hints.body: Try several permitted positive integers in the cube difference and check whether the resulting integers have factors other than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and themselves. Use any example you find to identify the earliest failed implication.
hints.recap: A single admissible counterexample disproves a universal numerical claim.
hints.pitfall: Do not name the last line as the first error without checking where its justification first fails.
hints.pause: Find and verify a numerical test, then locate the first inference it contradicts.

recall.reminder: Judge the chain of reasoning separately from the truth of its conclusion.

solution:
The expansion and subtraction in I and II are correct. In III the quadratic 3x2+3x+1 has discriminant 9−12=−3, so it cannot factor into real linear factors, and in particular cannot factor into integer-coefficient linear factors.

But irreducibility of a polynomial does not mean that every integer value it takes is prime. At x=5, the difference is 63−53=91=7×13.

The unsupported step from polynomial factorisation to factorisation of every numerical value first occurs in IV. Answer: F.
knowledgePattern: Distinguish polynomial irreducibility from primality of individual values
